title: Sunny and the Big Wind | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka experiences a warm big wind sweeping through the bush, making the whole forest dance with spinning leaves and swaying branches before it hushes to a peaceful whisper. A lively yet calming bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The wind arrived all at once.

One moment the bush was still. The next, everything was moving.

Leaves spun in little spirals. Tall grasses bent flat. Branches bowed and waved as if greeting someone very old and very large.

Little Sunny the quokka stood in the middle of it all, her round ears pressed back, her fur rippling, her eyes bright.

The wind was warm. That was the surprising thing. She had expected cold, but the wind was warm as breath, warm as a blanket pulled close.

It rushed past her ears with a sound like the sea — a long, deep whoooosh — and she leaned into it just a little, letting it hold her.

A seed pod sailed past, spinning.

Three leaves tumbled upward, spiralling into the sky.

Sunny watched them go, turning slowly on the spot to follow their paths.

Then, just as suddenly as it had come — the wind eased.

One gust. Two. Then softer. Then quieter.

Until it was just a whisper.

The bush settled. Leaves drifted back down. The grass stood up again, slowly.

Everything was still. But different — rearranged and refreshed, as if the bush had shaken itself awake and then decided to go back to sleep.

Sunny curled into the roots of a big banksia tree, the last of the warm wind sighing through the branches above her.

She closed her eyes and let the whisper carry her to sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, big wind. Goodnight, little one.
